_meta.indication: GIAPREZA increases blood pressure in adults with septic or other distributive shock.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: ATHOS-3 (Angiotensin II for the Treatment of High-Output Shock; study LJ501-CRH01)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal randomized controlled trial (single adequate and well-controlled trial supporting the NDA)
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized (1:1) multicenter trial conducted under a special protocol assessment (SPA), with study drug titrated to a target mean arterial pressure (MAP).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with septic or other distributive (catechol-resistant) shock who remained hypotensive (MAP 55 to 70 mmHg) despite fluid and vasopressor therapy; 91% had septic shock.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: percentage of subjects achieving a MAP ≥ 75 mmHg or a ≥ 10 mmHg increase in MAP without an increase in baseline vasopressor therapy at 3 hours.
pivotal_trials.n: 321 patients in the mITT population (163 GIAPREZA, 158 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint achieved by 70% (114/163) on GIAPREZA vs 23% (37/158) on placebo (OR=7.95, 95% CI 4.76, 13.3, p=2.54E-15). Day-28 mortality 46% vs 54% (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.57–1.07), not statistically significant.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were thromboembolic events. Higher incidence of arterial and venous thrombotic/thromboembolic events vs placebo (13% vs 5%), including deep vein thrombosis (4.3% vs 0.0%). Other AEs: thrombocytopenia (9.8% vs 7.0%), tachycardia (8.6% vs 5.7%), fungal infection (6.1% vs 1.3%).
target_moa: Angiotensin II is a naturally occurring peptide hormone of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system that raises blood pressure by vasoconstriction and increased aldosterone release, acting via the G-protein-coupled angiotensin II receptor type 1 on vascular smooth muscle cells.
modality: Peptide (synthetic human angiotensin II, an 8-amino-acid peptide hormone)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; there were no issues requiring AC consideration.

summary.text: The NDA was submitted 6/29/2017 as a new molecular entity and granted Priority Review (PDUFA goal 2/28/2018). Approval was a first-cycle, full (traditional) approval based on the single adequate and well-controlled trial ATHOS-3, conducted under a special protocol assessment. No advisory committee was convened; pediatric studies were deferred as required postmarketing studies under PREA.

The applicant conducted one double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized, multicenter trial (LJ501-CRH01, “ATHOS-3”) under a SPA agreement.
There are no issues that require consideration by an AC, and no AC meeting has been scheduled.
We are deferring submission of your pediatric studies until February 2022, because this product is ready for approval for use in adults and the pediatric studies have not been completed.
